lines.en: Yes, please. **What can we see** in the city?
lines.pt: Sim, por favor. O que podemos ver na cidade?

lines.en: You can see the old tower and the river park.
lines.pt: Vocês podem ver a torre antiga e o parque do rio.

lines.en: **Is it open today?** I mean the tower.
lines.pt: Está aberta hoje? Quero dizer, a torre.

lines.en: **How do we get to** the tower?
Take bus 12. It’s ten minutes from here.
lines.pt: Peguem o ônibus 12. São dez minutos daqui.

lines.en: Yes, a one-day pass is $25. It includes the tower and a museum.
lines.pt: Sim, o passe de um dia custa 25 dólares. Inclui a torre e um museu.

lines.en: Great, **we’ll take** two. And a map, please!
lines.pt: Ótimo, vamos levar dois. E um mapa, por favor!

pages.title: Tourist information

situation.text: You arrive in a new city with a friend. You go to the tourist information desk to ask what to see, if a place is open and how to get there.

pages.goal: By the end of the class you can ask a tourist desk what to see, if a place is open today, how to get there and about a pass.
canDo: Ask: How do we get to…?
success: I ask if it is open.
I ask how to get there.
I ask about a pass or a map.
pages.think: When you arrive in a new city, what do you want to know first? Where do you look for information?

teach.goal: Abrir pela situação real: balcão de informações turísticas. Reaproveita direções de aulas anteriores sem retomar a lição.
solo: Pergunte como o aluno busca informações ao chegar em uma cidade (app, mapa, balcão).
Mostre os 4 critérios de sucesso.
group: Cada aluno cita um lugar turístico de que gosta.
extra: Do you use a paper map or your phone?
support: Aceite respostas curtas e reformule em inglês.

pages.title: Cultural snapshot — tourist offices and passes
pages.intro: Many cities have a visitor center or tourist information desk. Look at the cards and guess what you can get there.

cards.note: Visitor centers often give maps and tell you what is near.
Places have opening hours; it is smart to ask “Is it open today?”
A pass can include several places in one ticket for a day or more.

qs.q: What can you ask at a tourist desk?
qs.pt: O que você pode perguntar no balcão de turismo?

levels.A2: What can we see, and is it open today?
levels.B1: You can ask what to see, opening hours, directions and prices.
levels.B2: You can ask for recommendations, opening hours, routes and whether a pass is worth it.

qs.q: Why is “Is it open today?” useful?
qs.pt: Por que “Is it open today?” é útil?

levels.A2: Some places are closed on some days.
levels.B1: Opening days and hours change, so it avoids a wasted trip.
levels.B2: Hours vary by day and season, so checking saves time.

qs.pt: O que é um city pass?

levels.B1: A pass that includes several attractions, sometimes with transport.
levels.B2: A bundle that can save money if you plan to visit several attractions.

pages.compare: In Brazil, many cities also have a tourist information point (posto de informações turísticas) and people ask for maps and tips. What do you ask for when you travel?

teach.goal: Mostrar o que se faz em um balcão de turismo: mapa, horários e passe. Não cite preços ou empresas reais.
solo: Mostre os cartões e peça hipóteses.
Compare com os postos de turismo no Brasil.
group: Cada aluno escolhe um cartão e explica.
answers: Q1: o que ver, horários, como chegar.
Q2: evita ir a um lugar fechado.
Q3: um bilhete para vários lugares.
extra: Is a free map useful today?
stretch: B2: quando um passe vale a pena e quando não?

teach.goal: Entender a situação e 4 informações: lugar, horário, ônibus e preço do passe.
solo: Esconda o texto. 1ª escuta: onde ela está.
2ª escuta: tower, 5 p.m., bus 12, $25.
Mostre o texto depois.

pages.title: Pronunciation lab — question intonation
pages.tip: Yes/no questions go up at the end: “Is it open today?” ↗. Questions with what, how or where usually go down: “How do we get to the tower?” ↘.

items.say: How do we get to the tower?
items.linked: HOW do we GET to the TOW·er? ↘

opts: What can we see? (voice up, surprised)

own.prompt: Write one yes/no question and one what/how question about a place.
own.criteria: Say them. Yes/no: voice goes up. What/how: voice goes down.

teach.goal: UM fenômeno: entonação de perguntas (sim/não sobe, what/how desce).
solo: Faça gestos com a mão subindo e descendo.
Peça que o aluno faça as duas perguntas.
answers: Identify 1: Is it open today? (up) · Identify 2: What can we see? (down)

errors.w: Is it open today? com voz descendo.

support: Reduza a velocidade e use a mão.

pages.title: Personalized roleplay — at the tourist desk

brief.teacher: You are the clerk at the tourist desk. Change the plan during the scene!
brief.student: You are the tourist: ask what to see, if it is open and how to get there.

orders: Ask about a park and the way to get there
Ask about a city pass and a map
complications: The place is closed today: ask for another idea.
The clerk says it is far: ask how to go.
The clerk speaks too fast: ask to repeat.
You need a map: ask politely.
success: I ask if it is open.
I ask how to get there.

teach.goal: Balcão de turismo com complicação e três rodadas com menos apoio.
solo: Use uma cidade real que o aluno quer visitar.
Rodada 1 com chunks; 2 palavras-chave; 3 sem roteiro.
Anote 2–3 correções.
stretch: Pedir uma sugestão de restaurante perto do museu.

rounds.hint: Is it open today? / It’s open until…

rounds.hint: How do we get to…? / Take…

b.title: Clerk B (knows transport)

group: Troque os pares a cada rodada.
Cada aluno faz ≥1 pergunta e ≥1 resposta.

pages.goal: Each group plans one day in a city: what to see, opening hours and how to get there.

missions.constraint: Use “How do we get to…?” twice.

teach.goal: Resolver um plano de dia na cidade com o inglês.
group: Cada grupo recebe papel, restrição e frase inicial. Alterne atendente e turista.
Rodada 1 com apoio, 2 palavras-chave, 3 sem roteiro.
answers: Modelo: “What can we see?” → “The tower.” → “Is it open today?” → “Yes, until 5.” → “How do we get there?”

pages.title: Writing — a small real-life task
pages.task: Write a short message to a hotel or a friend to ask about a place to visit. Ask what to see, if it is open and how to get there.
pages.model: Hello! We are visitors in your city. What can we see near the hotel? Is the museum open on Sunday? How do we get there from the hotel? Thank you!
checklist: I asked about hours or directions.
pages.tip: Fix only 2–3 priority points. Show a more natural way to say the same idea.

teach.goal: Produção escrita curta ligada à situação.
solo: Peça a mensagem; corrija 2–3 pontos.

errors.r: How do we get to the museum?

support: Dê o modelo e peça que troquem os dados.

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: The structure stays the same; language complexity and autonomy grow.

ladder.say: What can we see? Is it open today?
ladder.goal: Ask what to see and if it is open.

ladder.say: How do we get to the tower? Is there a bus?
We have only one day. Could you suggest a plan that includes the main sights?
We’d like to avoid the crowds, so is there a quieter time to visit the tower?
Rather than the usual tourist circuit, could you point us toward something more local?
Anything off the beaten path that a visitor wouldn’t find in a guidebook would be most welcome.

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own.
